Nákupy posedlá čtyřicátnice ujíždí na slevových akcích s takovou vášní, že ani nepostřehne, jak si její muž nachází během jejího nákupního maratonu mladší model. Se zhrzeným egem a bez kreditky úspěšného manžela, začíná Klára znovu od piky. Hledá novou práci, nového muže, ale především samu sebe.

programme.title: Hercule Poirot - Hodiny
programme.desc: Stárnoucí herec Sir Charles Cartwright uspořádá pro své přátele a známé večírek, který však skončí smrtí jednoho z nich. Hercule Poirot, který byl rovněž mezi pozvanými, odmítá uvěřit ve vraždu, protože si vůbec neumí představit, jak by mohla být spáchána a vše pokládá za nešťastnou náhodu. Když však dojde k dalšímu podobnému úmrtí, musí svůj úsudek radikálně opravit a vydat se po stopách nelítostného vraha.

programme.title: Slečna Marplová - Modrá pelargonie
programme.desc: V případě smrti pověrčivé ženy, jejíž příčinou byl zdánlivě šok vyvolaný předpovědí, kterou jí krátce předtím sdělilo médium, tuší slečna Marplová, že vše není tak, jak to vypadá.

programme.title: Ślećna Scarletova - Pandořina skříňka
programme.desc: Sestra pohřešované ženy si najme Elizu, aby ji našla, ale když policie případ uzavře, vznikne mezi Elizou a Vévodou nové napětí.

programme.title: Vraždy v Oxfordu
programme.desc: Když je ve svém domě nalezena oběšená žena z Oxfordu, Lewis a Hathaway odhalí mnohem temnější případ vraždy, než jaký naznačuje původní verdikt o sebevraždě.

programme.title: Slečna Marplová - Rozbité zrcadlo
programme.desc: Znepokojená hollywoodská hvězda a její manžel se právě přestěhovali do St. Mary Mead, ale jejich příjezd zastíní tragédie. Jeden z fanoušků zemře během zahradní slavnosti na otravu jedem.

programme.title: Hercule Poirot - Sloni mají paměť
programme.desc: Ariadnu Oliverovou přepadne na předávání literárních cen jistá paní Burton-Coxová a vyptává se známé spisovatelky na jednu z mnoha jejích kmotřenek, Celii Ravenscroftovou, na niž si paní Oliverová jen sotva pamatuje. Paní Burton-Coxová však ještě více překvapí, když se zeptá: „Zabil její otec její matku, nebo zabila matka jejího otce?“ a připomene tak Ariadně tragédii, při které byli oba rodiče Celie zastřeleni. Kdo však vystřelil první a následně spáchal sebevraždu, zůstalo záhadou.

programme.title: Ślećna Scarletova - Černá můra čarodějnice
programme.desc: Cenný nákres nedávného zesnulého Charlese Darwina byl ukraden a Eliza je najata pojišťovnou, aby jej našla. Brzy však dojde ke zvratu.

programme.title: Zločiny z vřesovišť - Skryté hlubiny
programme.desc: Vera Stanhopeová stojí před dvěma krátce po sobě spáchanými vraždami, jejichž oběti byly naaranžovány způsobem, připomínajícím umělecké instalace - ve vodě plné krásných květin. Podezřelých je mnoho a vrah zatím chystá další zrůdné výtvarné dílo...

programme.title: Slečna Fisherová a záhada Hrobky slz
programme.desc: Poté, co slečna Fisherová zachrání beduínskou dívku z vězení v Jeruzalémě, začne se rozplétat dávná záhada. Ta zahrnuje drahocenný smaragd, starou kletbu a pravdu týkající se tajemného zmizení dívčina kmene…

programme.title: Borrego
programme.desc: Mladý botanik se přestěhuje do malého pouštního městečka, aby zde studoval invazivní druh rostliny. Během výzkumu přijíždí na pomoc spadlému letadlu, aby se vzápětí ocitla v zajetí nezkušeného drogového překupníka, který ji nutí, aby vedla cestu přes dusnou poušť k jeho výsadku. Do pátrání je vtažen místní šerif, jehož vzpurná dcera se vydává hledat zmizelou botaničku, přičemž ji po celou dobu pronásleduje místní příjemce drog.

programme.title: Sidney Hall
programme.desc: Nehledě na mladý věk projevuje Sidney Hall zralý talent pro psaní. Jeho školní eseje ukazují hrozby, které některé odrazují, avšak jeden učitel rozpozná talent a vyzývá Sidneyho, aby se dal na spisovatelskou dráhu. Úspěchy s prvním románem učiní ze Sidneyho celebritu, ačkoli jeho antiutopie z předměstí vyvolává tragické reakce u některých mladých čtenářů a zavleče jeho jméno do skandálu.

programme.title: Sidney Hall
programme.desc: Nehledě na mladý věk projevuje Sidney Hall zralý talent pro psaní. Jeho školní eseje ukazují hrozby, které některé odrazují, avšak jeden učitel rozpozná talent a vyzývá Sidneyho, aby se dal na spisovatelskou dráhu. Úspěchy s prvním románem učiní ze Sidneyho celebritu, ačkoli jeho antiutopie z předměstí vyvolává tragické reakce u některých mladých čtenářů a zavleče jeho jméno do skandálu.

programme.title: Sucho
programme.desc: Dva sousedské klany a dva různé přístupy k životu. Co se stane, když do napjatých vztahů dvou dominantních otců zasáhne láska vlastních dětí? Zatímco Josef nutí svou rodinu ke svéráznému způsobu života na ostrůvku vegetace mezi monokulturními Viktorovými lány, Míra je zamilovaný do Josefovy dcery Žofky. Aby získal její sympatie, musí s otcem bojovat. Synova revolta staví Viktora do nové situace. I Josef zklamaný důsledky vlastních životních postojů má možnost leccos přehodnotit.

programme.title: Šťastná
programme.desc: Hlavní hrdinka Viktorie Šťastná odjíždí studovat do Prahy hereckou akademii. Záhy však zjišťuje, že se její původní ideály nesetkávají s realitou. Dostává se do party protřelých studentek, které pojímají hereckou kariéru zcela osobitým způsobem. Co všechno je Viky ochotná udělat pro úspěch.

programme.title: Vraždy v Oxfordu
programme.desc: Když je ve svém domě nalezena oběšená žena z Oxfordu, Lewis a Hathaway odhalí mnohem temnější případ vraždy, než jaký naznačuje původní verdikt o sebevraždě.

programme.title: Vraždy v Oxfordu
programme.desc: Inspektor Lewis vyšetřuje vraždu zaměstnance knihovny, který propadl hazardu. Zanedlouho je nalezena další mrtvola, tentokrát mladé studentky umění. Mají tyto případy nějakou souvislost?

programme.title: Slečna Marplová - Rozbité zrcadlo
programme.desc: Znepokojená hollywoodská hvězda a její manžel se právě přestěhovali do St. Mary Mead, ale jejich příjezd zastíní tragédie. Jeden z fanoušků zemře během zahradní slavnosti na otravu jedem.

programme.title: Vražedné záhady slečny Fisherové - Kokainové blues
programme.desc: Ctihodná slečna Phryne Fisherová vyrazí do Melbourne. Téměř okamžitě se ocitá v samém srdci záhadného případu.

programme.title: Slečna Marplová - Karibské tajemství
programme.desc: Slečna Marplová se zaplete do případy plného intrik a černé magie. Muž, který se chlubil tím, že má fotografii, na níž je vrah, zemře za podezřelých okolností.

programme.title: Hercule Poirot - Velká čtyřka
programme.desc: Setkání dávných přátel obvykle bývá důvodem k radosti, tentokrát je tomu ovšem jinak. Inspektor Japp, povýšený mezitím na zástupce komisaře, slečna Lemonová a kapitán Hastings se scházejí na pohřbu svého drahého přítele Hercula Poirota a rekapitulují události posledních čtyř týdnů, které vedly k jeho předčasné smrti.

programme.title: Vraždy pro slečnu Fisherovou - Vražda v obchodním domě - Část 1
programme.desc: V Melbourne na módní přehlídce došlo ke zločinu. Modelka Barbie Jonesová byla uškrcena a její tělo objeveno přímo během show Florence Asterové, také členky Klubu dobrodružek, v obchodním domě. Vyšetřování se ujímá detektive James Steed. Florence je z neúspěchu přehlídky zničená a potřebuje dobrého detektiva.

programme.title: Zločiny z vřesovišť - Stíny vzpomínek
programme.desc: Je to už pěkná řádka let, co bylo nalezeno tělo uškrcené Abigail Mantelové. Ze zločinu byla obviněna nadaná hudebnice Jeanie Longová, milenka vlivného podnikatele a ovdovělého otce oběti. Soudce neuvěřil jejímu tvrzení, že se v inkriminovaném dni nacházela v Londýně, a mladou ženu poslal na doživotí do vězení.

programme.title: V ústraní
programme.desc: Doktorka Madeline Fayeová, úspěšná psychiatrička a autorka bestsellerů, hledá útočiště v plážovém domě svého bohatého otce, zatímco pracuje na své další knize. Začíná mít podezření, že ji pronásleduje bývalý pacient.

programme.title: Prípad mrtvých spoluzáku
programme.desc: Režisér Dušan Klein natočil podle archivních materiálů československé bezpečnosti film Případ mrtvých spolužáků. Jeho děj se odehrává v roce 1963, kdy do tehdejšího Československa přijíždí západoněmecký obchodník Friedrich Schmidt. Nikdo netuší, že tu má zpravodajské poslání.

programme.title: Penicka a Paraplícko
programme.desc: Nešťastně zamilovaný kasař Pěnička a prostitutka Anča, zvaná Paraplíčko, jsou známými členy pražské "galerky". Jejich případem se s pochopením pro lidské slabosti ujme sám rada Vacátko…

programme.title: Masaryk
programme.desc: Výpravné drama režiséra Julia Ševčíka přibližuje „neznámý“ výsek ze života českého diplomata Jana Masaryka. Deprimovaný, vnitřně rozpolcený syn prvního československého prezidenta po podepsání mnichovské dohody odjede do USA a skončí v sanatoriu, jež vede německý psychiatr Dr. Stein. Nový životní impulz mu dodá až seznámení s americkou novinářkou a spisovatelkou Marcií Davenportovou.

programme.title: Lilly Schönauer: A teď už je to láska
programme.desc: Mnichovská kardioložka Katja je šťastná. Má před sebou svatbu s bohatým konzultantam Richardem a navíc ji čeká povýšení v nemocnici. Nakonec je ale všechno jinak. Vedoucí kardiologického oddělení se nestane ona, ale její konkurent. A Richard na toto zklamání nereaguje tak empaticky, jak by si lékařka přála.

programme.title: Celebrity S.R.O.
programme.desc: Děj filmu nás zavede do blíže nejmenovaného studia se všemi typickými postavičkami tohoto světa rychloobrátkové zábavy. Mladí začínající herci se tu potkávají s neskutečně prudivými hereckými legendami, režisér přicházející se svými nápady naráží na lokty ostré producentky, která sleduje vlastní zájmy, technici tu a tam něco pokazí a vše by běželo ve svých obvyklých zajetých kolejích, kdyby režisér Tomáš, hlavní postava filmu, nepřišel s odvážným nápadem.

programme.title: Pet miliónu svedku
programme.desc: Nyní spatříme naivní připomínku toho, že televize kdysi vysílala i inscenace živě, avšak v tomto případě získal přímý přenos překvapivě kriminální rozměr. Během vysílání byl totiž zabit jeden z herců - a vidělo to všech oněch pět milionů lidí, kteří televizi sledovali. Vyšetřovatelé pak celou podezřelou událost znovu rekonstruují, aby se dopátrali, zda šlo o nešťastnou náhodu nebo promyšlený zločin...

programme.title: Deník shopaholičky
programme.desc: Také tak milujete nakupování? Zrychluje se Vám tep při slovech výprodej? Shopaholička Klára to má stejně. Nákupy posedlá čtyřicátnice ujíždí na slevových akcích s takovou vášní, že ani nepostřehne, jak si její muž nachází během jejího nákupního maratonu mladší model. Se zhrzeným egem a bez kreditky úspěšného manžela, začíná Klára znovu od piky. Hledá novou práci, nového muže, ale především samu sebe.

programme.title: Zločiny z vřesovišť - Pachuť smrti
programme.desc: Vera Stanhopeová vede kriminalistický tým v severoanglickém Northumberlandu. Její způsob vyšetřování je nezvyklý, ale účinný. Místo na shromažďování faktů se soustředí spíše na vcítění se do duší a vztahů všech zainteresovaných a z toho pak činí své závěry.

programme.title: Zločiny z vřesovišť - Dávná tajemství
programme.desc: Vera Stanhopeová vede kriminalistický tým v severoanglickém Northumberlandu. Její způsob vyšetřování je nezvyklý, ale účinný. Místo na shromažďování faktů se soustředí spíše na vcítění se do duší a vztahů všech zainteresovaných a z toho pak činí své závěry.

programme.title: Hercule Poirot - Viděla jsem vraždu
programme.desc: Orient expres, luxusní vlak, projíždějící celou Evropou, se jedné mrazivé noci stává dějištěm případu, k jehož vyřešení musí Hercule Poirot, který se čirou náhodou ocitl mezi jeho pasažéry, zapojit veškerý svůj důvtip a genialitu. Má k tomu dostatek času, protože vlaku, uvězněnému sněhovou kalamitou kdesi v srbském vnitrozemí, nezbývá než trpělivě čekat na vysvobození ze závějí.

programme.title: Hercule Poirot - Vražda v Orient expresu
programme.desc: Když vcházela písařka Sheila Webbová do domu slečny Pebmarshové, netušila, jaké překvapení ji čeká. Na podlaze za pohovkou ležel mrtvý muž a zcela prokazatelně nezemřel přirozenou smrtí. A aby té smůly nebylo dost, policejní inspektor Hardcastle si vzal do hlavy, že jej zavraždila právě ona. Naštěstí před domem narazila na mladého poručíka Racea, který slíbil, že jí pomůže. A důstojník britského námořnictva drží slovo. Obzvláště, může-li se spolehnout na pomoc geniálního Hercula Poirota.

programme.title: Hercule Poirot - Hodiny
programme.desc: Stárnoucí herec Sir Charles Cartwright uspořádá pro své přátele a známé večírek, který však skončí smrtí jednoho z nich. Hercule Poirot, který byl rovněž mezi pozvanými, odmítá uvěřit ve vraždu, protože si vůbec neumí představit, jak by mohla být spáchána a vše pokládá za nešťastnou náhodu. Když však dojde k dalšímu podobnému úmrtí, musí svůj úsudek radikálně opravit a vydat se po stopách nelítostného vraha.

programme.title: Superžena
programme.desc: Šest chlapů - scenáristů dostalo za úkol napsat filmovou povídku na téma: Jak si představujete superženu? Tato nevyčerpatelná studnice ženského světa dostává prostřednictvím scénáristů nečekaně překvapivé zápletky a interpretace. Setkáváme se s ženami v různých situacích, které na první pohled nemají s představou ženy v superlativech nic společného, a povídky jsou o to překvapivější...

programme.title: Chata na prodej
programme.desc: Rodiče prodávají starou chatu, pro kterou už nemají využití. Před předáním chaty novému majiteli se však matka (Ivana Chýlková) rozhodne uspořádat poslední pořádnou rodinnou slezinu. Zbytek příbuzenstva neprojevuje přílišné nadšení, tahle setkání bývají vždy dost náročná. Děda (Jan Kačer) už je duchem spíše nepřítomen, otec (David Vávra) tyto akce odmítá, syn (Jan Strejcovský) je věčně přiopilý a ironicky glosuje svět kolem sebe včetně rozpadajícího se vztahu s přítelkyní (Judit Bárdos).

programme.title: Nahota na prodej
programme.desc: Krátce po sametové revoluci se z kdekoho stává podnikatel. Obory podnikání se různí. Ať už jsou to legální formy, nebo naopak organizovaný zločin. Mladá studentka Nancy přijíždí do Prahy na stáž. Má české kořeny, a proto si zvolila Prahu. Společně s novinářem Egonem a bývalým policistou, nyní soukromým detektivem Poldou, pátrají po unesené šestnáctileté dívce. Její otec je zoufalý, ani policie mu nedokáže pomoci.

programme.title: The Pilgrim
programme.desc: Disguised as a priest, an escaped convict makes his way to Texas. He ends up in a small rural town where the townsfolk mistake him for their new church minister.

programme.title: Gregoire
programme.desc: Loosely based on real life events, Gregoire follows four young adults and the choices they make when put at a crossroads of their life. As they struggle to make choices, their paths cross with one another and their choices affect not only themselves, but their friends, and their families.

programme.title: The Strange Woman
programme.desc: In early 19th century New England, an attractive unscrupulous woman uses her beauty and wits to deceive and control the men around her.

programme.title: Mother
programme.desc: A teenaged girl witnesses her widowed mother's attempt to sustain her family.

programme.title: Joan of Arkansas
programme.desc: When the U.S. Space program requires an ordinary person to become the first human in space, the Saraback Computer chooses Joan Jones, a scatter brained, good natured klutz who works as a dental technician.

programme.title: Impact
programme.desc: A unfaithful wife plots with her lover to kill her husband, but the lover is accidentally killed instead. The husband stays in hiding and lets his wife be charged with conspiracy.

programme.title: Little Lord Fauntleroy
programme.desc: An American boy turns out to be the long-lost heir of a British fortune. He is sent to live with the cold and unsentimental lord who oversees the trust.

programme.title: Angel and the Bad Man
programme.desc: Notorious shootist and womanizer Quirt Evans' horse collapses as he passes a Quaker family's home. Quirt has been wounded, and the kindly family takes him in to nurse him back to health against the advice of others.

programme.title: Nel mio amore
programme.desc: The love story of a couple which, after the marriage and the birth of the first son, turns into hell. Taken from the novel Rispondimi by Susanna Tamaro.

programme.title: Sunny
programme.desc: The beautiful Anna Neagle stars as a circus performer who falls in love with a rich car dealer's son, against her family's wishes. Features some spirited dance numbers with Ray Bolger.

programme.title: Padre
programme.desc: Mourning the death of her father, Giulia is contacted by him from the other dimension.

programme.title: And Then There Were None
programme.desc: Seven guests, a newly hired personal secretary and two staff are gathered for a weekend on an isolated island by the hosts the Owens who are delayed. At dinner a record is played and the host's message alleges that all the people present are guilty of murder and suddenly the first of them is dead, then the next - It seems that one of them is the murderer but the leading person is always the person who is murdered next and at last only two people are left.

programme.title: Roaring Abyss
programme.desc: A sound journey accros the mountains, deserts and forests of Ethiopia and its cultural universe. Roaring Abyss will take you through an inedit collection of music recordings of unvaluable importance for the transmission and preservation of the African heritage.

programme.title: Quality Time
programme.desc: Five thirty-something men in as many separate segments struggle to grapple with the relentless absurdity of their respective existences.

programme.title: Frieda
programme.desc: A Royal Air Force pilot who was shot down during World War II returns home to his English village with his new bride. The trouble is that she is the German lady who helped him escape. Then her brother arrives.

programme.title: Footprints on the Moon
programme.desc: A woman is tormented by strange dreams of astronauts on the moon. She visits a deserted seaside town whose inhabitants know her although she does not know them.

programme.title: Lady Of Burlesque
programme.desc: After one member of their group is murdered, the performers at a burlesque house must work together to find out who the killer is before they strike again.

programme.title: Lady Of Burlesque
programme.desc: After one member of their group is murdered, the performers at a burlesque house must work together to find out who the killer is before they strike again.

programme.title: Went the Day Well?
programme.desc: The quiet village of Bramley End is taken over by German troops posing as Royal Engineers. Their task is to disrupt England's radar network in preparation for a full scale German invasion. Once the villagers discover the true identity of the troops, they do whatever they can to thwart the Nazis plans.

programme.title: Someone Behind the Door
programme.desc: A neurosurgeon with a cheating wife takes an amnesiac into his home and conditions him to believe that the cheating wife is his own and to take the "appropriate" action.

programme.title: Musashino Fujin
programme.desc: Set in post-war Japan, The Lady of Musashino tells the story of Michiko, a disillusioned young woman trapped in a loveless marriage. She confides in her younger cousin, Tsutomo, and the two become close, but decide not to consummate their affair. He instead becomes involved with the flirtatious Tomiko, who is also conducting an affair with Michiko's husband. When Michiko finds that her husband has abandoned her, she decides to take her fate into her own hands.

programme.title: Daughters, Wives and a Mother
programme.desc: Tashiro coincidentally meets his best friend Sugimoto in a bar very close to the apartment in which Sugimoto’s wayward wife is found dead. Although Tashiro is not a suspect in the police investigation, he is racked with guilt and confesses to his wife, Masako. In an effort to further relieve his tortured sense of guilt, he then confesses to Sugimoto. Neither his wife nor his friend can believe that he could have been involved.

programme.title: Smash-Up: The Story Of A Woman - The Story Of A Woman
programme.desc: A successful nightclub singer weds a struggling songwriter, but when his fame eclipses hers, she delves into alcoholism.

programme.title: People We Know Are Confused
programme.desc: Set in Vilnius, a modern city still in search for its relation to the past, three parallel stories with three average people marooned in a state of change, looking to the future with hope, but not letting go of constricting and reassuring fears of their past.

programme.title: Beneath The 12-Mile Reef
programme.desc: Fierce competition among sponge fishermen forces a Greek-American family to fish in the dangerous 12-mile reef area off the western coast of Florida.

programme.title: Too Late for Tears
programme.desc: Through a fluke circumstance, a ruthless woman stumbles across a suitcase filled with $60,000, and is determined to hold onto it even if it means murder.

programme.title: Rain

For a long time, the town had been divided, with the cattlemen and cowboys having one end of town to themselves, while townspeople occupied the other end. Mitchell liked it this way, it made things easier for him, and kept problems from arising between the two factions.

programme.title: The Admiral Was a Lady
programme.desc: Ex-WAVE encounters four fun-loving, work-hating men, all of whom want to marry her.

programme.title: My Favorite Brunette

When the oil and the money start gushing in, both Brad and Jim want to protect the land but Cherokee has different ideas. What started out as revenge for her father's death has turned into an obsession for wealth and power.

Driven by bravery (and sheer desperation) they flee to the country and, with the help of other workers, set up a farming community - a socialist mini-society. The newborn community suffers many hardships - drought, vicious raccoons and the long arm of the law - but ultimately pull together to reach a bread-based Utopia.

programme.title: The Passionate Plumber
programme.desc: Paris plumber Elmer Tuttle is enlisted by socialite Patricia Alden to help make her lover Tony Lagorce jealous. With the help of his friend Julius J. McCracken and through the high society contacts he has made through Patricia, Elmer hopes to find financing for his latest invention, a pistol with a range-finding light. Comic complications ensue when Elmer's effort to interest a military leader is misconstrued as an assassination attempt.

programme.title: Nabonga

programme.title: The Little Shop of Horrors

programme.title: Hell's House
programme.desc: Jimmy idolizes bootlegger Matt, and when he refuses to implicate his friend, he is sent to reform school. He befriends Shorty, a boy with a heart condition, and escapes to let the world know about the brutal conditions.

programme.title: Prelude to Murder

programme.title: Mr Wong - Doomed To Die

Of course, Captain Street arrests Dick, but reporter Bobbie Logan, the attractive thorn in Street's side, is so convinced he's wrong that she enlists the help of detective James Lee Wong to find the real killer.

However, not everybody is as easily swayed by their capricious leader, who eventually starts to question his own beliefs.

programme.title: She Should'A Said No

programme.title: The Mystery of Mr. Wong

programme.title: Behind Green Lights
programme.desc: An unscrupulous private investigator with a penchant for blackmail is found dead in a car and the leading suspect is Janet Bradley, the daughter of a mayoral candidate. With the election just weeks away, shady and ruthless individuals muscle the medical officer into switching the corpse with another body. Lieutenant Sam Carson, one of the few good apples in the bunch must find a way to get to the bottom of it all.

Today, paper contributes heavily to pollution—about 10% of greenhouse gases. The future? E-paper: the digital alternative to traditional paper.

programme.desc: Ray Mears journeys into the remote wilderness region of Arnhem land to the Cooper Creek Billabong. He’s there during the dry season and all the wild life is concentrated into a narrow stretch of water. He comes face to face with the dominant saltwater crocodile and watches as the croc manoeuvres a dead pig down river to a secret hiding place.

programme.title: Animal Embassy - Super Vet to the Rescue
programme.desc: As Loro Parque’s head vet, Jorge never knows from one day to the next what will come through his clinic. Ever seen a grown man hug a turtle? For Javier, Loro Parque’s Head of Environmental Affairs, it’s all part of the job!

programme.title: Animal Embassy - Clownfish and White Tigers
programme.desc: ‘Finding Nemo’ may have brought fame to the striped clownfish but their newfound popularity has sent worldwide numbers into decline. Now we follow the aquarium team as they initiate their very own breeding program with the hope of finding many more Nemos to come. Jorge has got a 200-pound problem on his hands. Lin Mao the white tiger has something wrong with his hip and the vets need to make a diagnosis.

programme.title: Meet My Wild Friend - Ambassadors
programme.desc: The First World War: soldiers from at least 20 countries were plunged in the hell of trenches and caught under a deluge of bombs. programme.title: Wild Ones - Fastest
programme.desc: The explosive sprinting Cheetah. The mighty bounding kangaroo. The horned and leaping wildebeest. The powerful and sure footed horse. Or the quick footed pronghorn. Which is the fastest over land? Cheetah - On Africa’s savannahs, predator and prey race at breathtaking speeds. Pronghorn - North America’s fastest, it sustains 60 km/h and can reach nearly 100. Wildebeest - Iconic endurance runners; calves walk within minutes and run within days.

programme.title: Wild Ones - Biggest
programme.desc: Fanged Spiders with their scurrying bites. The Scorpion with its deadly sting... A sinister cold bloodied crocodile. The hypnotizing venomous snake. Or the King of Beasts, the Lion? Which one is the most dangerous? Lion - With golden fur and regal mane, the lion reigns as the ‘King of Beasts’. Scorpions - In scorched deserts, danger awakens after sunset. Spiders - Masters of webs and venom, spiders haunt myth and imagination.

programme.title: The Blue Realm - Deep White
programme.desc: Believe it or not, many scuba divers want to see great whites up close, and photographers want dramatic shots. But how do you get the sharks to where you want them? For decades, it's been done by baiting, or “chumming” - attracting sharks with food. This practice is being questioned and banned in many countries because of a dramatic increase in shark attacks.

programme.title: Sarah Shark - Episode 6
programme.desc: Sarah travels to one of the top 10 dive destinations in Australia (Julian Rocks, Byron Bay, NSW) to dive with three species of Wobbegong Sharks within the Cape Byron Marine Park. She also conducts a street poll with members of the public to find out what they think about sharks.

programme.title: Race of Life - Reptillian
programme.desc: Crocodiles, descended from reptiles 250 million years ago, lurk just beneath the waterline, striking fear into prey. Turtles, among the oldest reptiles, use their shells for protection and camouflage across land, freshwater, and sea. Snakes, from rattlesnakes to dwarf pipe snakes, share traits like legless bodies and lidless eyes, relying on sun for warmth. The king cobra’s venom can kill an elephant. Lizards escape predators by shedding tails, which regrow differently.

programme.title: Race of Life - Defenses in the Race of Life
programme.desc: Predators use speed, teeth, poison, and trickery to survive, but prey animals have evolved fascinating defenses. While fleeing is common, others use deception and chemistry—camouflage, mimicry, and toxins. Insects mimic leaves, snakes play dead, fish fly, and toads have poisonous skin. Predator-prey dynamics form an evolutionary arms race, with each side adapting to outsmart the other. Defense mechanisms include claws, poison, camouflage, and foul sprays.

programme.title: On the Cities’ Rooftops - Tokyo
programme.desc: How is life on the city’s roofs? This series scales new heights, exploring apartment buildings, towers and monuments to discover a world full of unsuspected treasures : our rooftops. By day and night, the population changes on these heights. There are people who work here, people who live here, and others who come here to relax. The world’s rooftops are a continual hive of activity.

programme.title: Blue World - Shark Electrosensory Systems + Helmet Diving + Oil Rigs
programme.desc: Jonathan joins shark researcher Dr. Stephen Kajiura to test how well wild sharks can detect electrical fields in their environment. programme.title: Quirky Science - Episode 6
programme.desc: Rubber was first used by South American tribes for waterproofing and bouncing balls. Westerners struggled with melting rubber until Charles Goodyear discovered vulcanization, making rubber durable. This sparked the rubber boom, enriching cities like Manaus. Britain broke Brazil’s monopoly by smuggling seeds. Later, synthetic rubber and Kevlar were developed—Kevlar is so tough it can stop bullets. Rubber’s journey is full of quirky discoveries.

programme.title: Quirky Science - Episode 7
programme.desc: Canned food began with Napoleon’s contest to preserve food, won by Appert’s boiled, sealed bottles. The British later developed metal cans, though early ones exploded or caused illness. Can openers came 30 years later. Pasteur’s germ theory explained spoilage. Pressure-cooking improved taste, and now, ‘raddaperization’—zapping food—is the future. Canning evolved from battlefield necessity to high-tech preservation.

programme.title: Wow, I Never Knew That! - Grand Central Terminal, 120 volts, nachos

From the items you use every day to the phrases you use in conversation to the habits you’re so accustomed to, you’ll be fascinated to learn how they’ve all really come about! Learn how a pharmacist and an accountant created the most famous drink in the world, COCA COLA!

And all the spy action heroes use them, but where did the term gadget really come from?

According to Interpol, art theft is the fourth largest criminal trade, after the drug trade, the weapons trade and money laundering.

programme.title: Wonder - Phantoms
programme.desc: The Body Transfer Illusion tricks the brain into feeling ownership of a fake body part, like in the rubber hand experiment. The Autokinetic Effect makes stationary lights seem to move in darkness. The Moon Illusion causes the moon to appear larger near the horizon due to visual references. Geometric illusions distort shapes and lines through clever design. Stereoscopy lets us perceive depth by merging two flat images into one 3D view.

programme.title: Wonder - Art of Illusion
programme.desc: Animation creates motion from still images shown in rapid sequence. Aviation illusions affect pilots’ balance due to conflicting sensory input. The spinning dancer illusion shows bistable perception—viewers may see it spin in either direction. Mirages occur when light bends through layers of air at different temperatures. Rainbows form when sunlight refracts and reflects through water droplets, splitting light into visible colors.

Clownfish - Tropical oceans shimmer with dazzling marine life like the vibrant clownfish. Kangaroo - Australia’s countryside pulses with thousands of bounding kangaroos. Monarch Butterfly - Monarchs fill the skies, delicate and stunning in flight. Budgerigar - Social and lively, wild budgies flock in hundreds across Australia.

programme.desc: The legendary wild dingo, the iconic kangaroos, vicious feral cats, the delightfully bizarre platypus and the unmistakably cuddly koala - all call Australia home. Koala - Hidden high in gum trees, the koala is one of Australia’s most beloved animals. Dingo - Sleek, agile, and descended from wolves, dingoes are Australia’s top land carnivores. Kangaroo - With powerful legs and iconic bounds, kangaroos embody the spirit of Australia.

programme.title: The Blue Realm - Lions of the Deep
programme.desc: Since the 1970's, sea lion populations have declined more than 80% along the North Pacific coast. Scientists at the University of British Columbia and the Vancouver Aquarium are working together to help save Canada’s iconic and largest pinniped - the stellar sea lion To help understand why their numbers are dropping, researchers work with the highly intelligent mammals at a unique floating laboratory.

programme.title: Sarah Shark - Episode 1
programme.desc: Sarah travels to one of the top 10 dive destinations in Australia (Julian Rocks, Byron Bay, NSW) to dive with three species of Wobbegong Sharks within the Cape Byron Marine Park. She also conducts a street poll with members of the public to find out what they think about sharks.

programme.title: Race of Life - Underwater Predators
programme.desc: Most sea creatures are predators, from tiny fish to giant squid. Built to hunt and survive, they’ve evolved into efficient underwater war machines. Stonefish lie in wait, disguised, while sharks, barracuda, and moray eels hunt with speed and precision. Reef fish must dodge lightning-fast barracuda and graceful but deadly moray eels. Lionfish use venomous spines, and stonefish can swallow prey whole.

programme.title: Race of Life - Underwater Prey's Defenses
programme.desc: The ocean is a harsh world where survival depends on feeding and avoiding predators. Sea creatures use camouflage, bright colors, venom, and group behavior for protection. Some hide, others rely on safety in numbers. Even venomous animals must stay alert. From top predators to bottom feeders, each species has evolved unique strategies. Defense includes toxins, teeth, mimicry, and camouflage.

programme.title: On the Cities’ Rooftops - Buenos Aires
programme.desc: How is life on the city’s roofs? This series scales new heights, exploring apartment buildings, towers and monuments to discover a world full of unsuspected treasures : our rooftops. By day and night, the population changes on these heights. There are people who work here, people who live here, and others who come here to relax. The world’s rooftops are a continual hive of activity.

programme.desc: In the series pilot, host Jonathan Bird travels to the Bahamas, where diver interactions with Tiger sharks have become up close and personal. These large and dangerous animals are not only being hand-fed, but actually handled by divers. Jonathan learns how to flip a Tiger shark from experienced shark handlers. Next, Jonathan investigates the Crystal Cave of Abaco, Bahamas…considered the most highly-ornamented underwater cave in the world!

programme.title: Blue World - Muck Driving in Florida + Iceland… The World's Clearest Water
programme.desc: Jonathan travels to Iceland to investigate a giant crack in the ground filled with frigid runoff from melting glaciers. It’s rumored to be the clearest water in the world. Next, he heads down to sunny Florida, not to dive a coral reef or a spectacular shipwreck, but to dive in shallow, murky water under a busy bridge. This secret spot is home to some of the ocean’s most remarkable, and weird, animals.

programme.title: Quirky Science - Episode 8
programme.desc: Medical history is full of odd cures—like bloodletting, which still helps in rare cases. Germs were once doubted until a doctor spotted bacteria between his teeth. Fleming later discovered antibiotics by accident. But now, ‘superbugs’ threaten this miracle cure. Refrigeration, once deadly due to toxic gases, evolved thanks to pressure-cooking and may soon use sound waves. From leeches to lab breakthroughs, medicine keeps evolving—what’s next?

programme.title: Quirky Science - Episode 9
programme.desc: The Internet began in 1969 as a Cold War military tool for secure communication. Email followed in 1972. Decades later, Tim Berners-Lee introduced the World Wide Web, linking documents and revolutionizing public access. His idea, once called “vague but exciting,” reshaped how we share, protest, and connect. Now, with Web 3.0 on the horizon, the Internet may evolve to understand human needs—what’s next in this digital journey?

programme.title: Wow, I Never Knew That! - Monopoly, area codes, tuxedo
programme.desc: Coca Cola, Slinky, Frisbee Take a trip to the Jersey Shore and learn how one of its famous boardwalks helped to inspire the iconic board game of Monopoly. And how did a donkey and an elephant become associated with politics? Plus, what’s the difference between top grain leather and full grain leather?

programme.title: Wow, I Never Knew That! - Zamboni ice resurfacing machine, pistachio nuts, stars
programme.desc: Coca Cola, Slinky, Frisbee If you have ever gone to a hockey game, or gone ice-skating, there is one revolutionary machine that helps keep the fun and action going! And that’s all thanks to the Zamboni® Ice Resurfacing Machine. You’ll learn how and why it was invented! And ever notice some pistachio nuts are red in color? We’ll throw up the red flag and explain why the color is simply a cover up!

And recent discoveries suggest that the number of stars in our galaxy alone, the Milky Way, may exceed 200 billion. Just what are these citizens of the night sky?

programme.title: New Frontier - The Dark Side
programme.desc: Perhaps that American politician was right. There are indeed things we know we don’t know. For instance, cosmologically speaking, we know we don’t know much - and certainly not nearly enough - about two of the enduring mysteries of the Universe. Dark Matter and Dark Energy, it’s little wonder that scientists are devoting so much grey matter and energy of their own to finding out as much as they can.

programme.title: Stolen Treasures - Episode 1
programme.desc: It’s the biggest museum in the world…the museum of artworks stolen over the centuries and never rediscovered. These works haunt the nightmares of their owners, and occupy the days of hundreds of police officers across the world, as well as those of a handful of private agencies; no country or museum of importance can claim to have been spared. According to Interpol, art theft is the fourth largest criminal trade, after the drug trade, the weapons trade and money laundering.

programme.title: Wonder - Phenomenal
programme.desc: Iridescence causes surfaces to reflect shifting colors due to light interference. Chemiluminescence produces light via chemical reactions, while bioluminescence does the same in living organisms using luciferin and luciferase. Gemstone colors come from structural elements or impurities affecting light absorption. Mechanical plant defenses include thorns, spines, and microscopic features that help plants survive threats.

programme.title: Wonder - Sensory Tricks
programme.desc: Vear is when visuals trigger imagined sounds, like the silent thud in the jumping pylon illusion. Retinal fatigue causes afterimages after staring at one color too long. The Müller-Lyer illusion tricks us into seeing equal lines as different lengths due to arrowheads. The Ames Room distorts size perception through skewed architecture. Synesthesia links senses—some people see colors when hearing sounds due to hyperconnected neurons.

We’ll tour one of the most stunning buildings in the frontier west at the Idaho State Capitol, dance all night with the Basques at the Basque museum and cultural center, soar to new heights at the Warhawk Air Museum in Nampa, and get a shiver down our spines at the Idaho state penitentiary.

programme.title: Travel Thru History - Space Coast
programme.desc: In this episode we visit the Kennedy Space Center located on Florida’s famous “Space Coast.” We’ll speak to NASA engineers about the past, present and future of American space travel, as well as take a look at the attractions KSC has to offer.

programme.title: Nature's Force - Episode 5
programme.desc: Snow is a fascinating world of crystals that animals, plants, and humans have had to adapt to, in order to benefit from its best and survive its worst attributes. Some communities live with Tornadoes by building homes with survival features and rather than get out of their paths, they rely on warning systems and classifications. And behind all great weather events is Wind, find out how and why it can change from a gentle breeze into a devastating gale force and where does it go?

programme.title: Nature's Force - Episode 6
programme.desc: What is La Nina and how is it being monitored? Find out the effects and the reach that this system is influencing. How did Indian Summer get its name and what is the science behind the phenomenon? Winter is the season that has the biggest effect on the planet, animal behaviour and often brings out the worst that nature can bring. Nature’s Halo is a magical sight with a scientific explanation.

programme.title: Big Coast - Season 12 - Hartley Bay Humpbacks and Chinook
programme.desc: Humpback Whales, perfect water, summer sunshine and one of the finest fishing Chinook Salmon solo fishing days!

programme.title: Wild Australia with Ray Mears - Episode 2
programme.desc: Ray Mears journeys into the remote wilderness region of Arnhem land to the Cooper Creek Billabong. He’s there during the dry season and all the wild life is concentrated into a narrow stretch of water. He comes face to face with the dominant saltwater crocodile and watches as the croc manoeuvres a dead pig down river to a secret hiding place.

programme.title: Journeys in India - Nepal - Kathmandu and Chitwan National Park
programme.desc: Just north of India is a land steeped in mystery—Nepal. Bill tours the city of Kathmandu, visits the World Heritage temple complexes, and walks along the city streets, where ancient and modern vie for space. We fly around Mount Everest, arguably the world’s most famous mountain, before heading into Chitwan National Park. In Chitwan, Bill searches for tigers from the back of an elephant and observes the myriad of wildlife that call the park home.

programme.title: Journeys in India - Ahmedabad - Land of Gandhi
programme.desc: There is no figure in Indian history that rivals Gandhi. Bill explores the land Gandhi called home and in the process, learns about the man himself. But Ahmedabad is more than Gandhi…its rich history and unusual architecture is revealed.

programme.title: Journeys in Africa - Tarangire - Land of the elephant
programme.desc: This is definitely the land of the elephant. Large herds of pachyderms roam this marshy park putting on a show for whoever wants to watch. But that’s not the only big boys of this park—buffalo, lion and a host of hoofed game make this a wonder to behold.

programme.title: Journeys in Africa - Nakuru National Park - Wonderland of Africa
programme.desc: This under-visited, and far western Kenyan park area, is renowned for its giant flamingo gatherings that literally turn lakes pink. We explore these many parks on foot, in a safari vehicle and on horseback searching out the local legends that have marked this region the death zone. Our host faces imminent doom in three unique parks in this fast-paced episode.

programme.title: Nomads - Alaska Big Mountain Extreme Skiing
programme.desc: Alaska is known for it's Alaskan Pipeline and the best heli-skiing this episode takes us deep into mountain lines as we try to out run avalanches.

programme.title: Nomads - Sub Zero - Freestyle Snowmobile Madness
programme.desc: A look into the world and culture of snowmobiling; the fans, the lifestyle and the sport.

programme.title: Dream Journey - Belize
programme.desc: February 2017 saw me embark upon a travel expedition through Scotland, Poland, France, Mexico, Belize and, (alas!), back. Not only was it the first time I ventured out to Central America, but also the first time I seriously pushed my bravery boundaries to do a whole lot of things I'd never tried before. I defeated my life-long fear of scubadiving and skydiving, (the Carribbean vistas do help!

programme.title: Of Boats and Men - Episode 9
programme.desc: Travelling by boat bears a priceless sense of Freedom and offers endless new vistas to all passengers. Across waterways around the world Boats are an essential tool of daily life whether they carry goods, serve as utilities or services in remote areas.

programme.title: Show Me Where You Live - Season 2 - Chile Chiloe, Wood Culture
programme.desc: Show me where you live is a documentary series that aims to answer the following question: How can human beings claim ownership to a space so that they can live safely within it, function as a society, and above all be in harmony with the environment around them? As we discover cultures and emblematic populations, we follow Philippe Simay who is at the heart of Inhabiting the World and represents its identity and originality.

programme.title: Yves Saint Laurent - Firestarter
programme.desc: A documentary of a true pioneer of fashion. Sabbatical Entertainment celebrates one of the most influential designers ever as we explore the designer's unparalleled professional acclaim, as well as his fascinating and tumultuous personal life. Yves Saint Laurent can be credited with both spurring the couture's rise in the 1960s as well as the tuxedo suit for women. He was able to adapt his style to accommodate the changes in fashion during his entire career.

programme.title: For Our Eyes Only
programme.desc: In “For Our Eyes Only,” get to know all the actors who have embodied the super spy: Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan, and Daniel Craig, their similarities and characteristics that differentiate each one when exhibiting his well-known charm, class and elegance, combined with physical and mental prowess, that makes 007 a real life super hero.

programme.title: Berber: A Quest For Water
programme.desc: A Quest For Water In the remote valleys of the Atlas range in Morocco, lies a village Tizi Anoucheg, where water is a rare resource. Berbers are the only people to be found in this harsh environment. They convert the red and dried valleys into a lush green using ancestral irrigation methods. With climate change threatening their very existence one man rises to the occasion & tries to solve the severe water problem.

programme.title: The World's Greatest Carnivals: Quebec Winter Carnival - Quebec Winter Carnival
programme.desc: This 3D documentary special takes us to one of the most colourful and elaborate celebrations on earth where both human creativity and glorious cultures come together. The Quebec Winter Carnival is the world’s largest winter Carnival. It celebrates everything about winter with all sorts of unique competitions and celebrations - from Canoe races across the St. Lawrence River to horse racing with sleds, dog-sledding, skating, ice sculptures, food, music and fun.

programme.title: Volcanic Planet
programme.desc: Volcanoes are the most extreme, dramatic, and explosive forces of nature on our planet. Volcanoes have produced many of the most valuable minerals - and most of the arable soil on earth. Every day, they are exploding around the world. When the Yellowstone Super Volcano blows (and it is now 48,000 years overdue to do so), it will destroy most of life on North America.

programme.title: The Subversives
programme.desc: Theo van Boven becomes Director of Human Rights for the UN in 1977, where it was impossible to even name a country for gross violations. No bureaucrat, he battles the most repressive regimes of the late 20th century, such as Chile and Argentina and opens the UN door for the first time to "subversive" survivors from across the world. Risking everything, he even takes on the US and the Secretary General.

programme.title: The Subversives

programme.title: Vacaciones con Fidel
programme.desc: Tristan is a journalist with deep political convictions who worked for years doing journalistic research. Once married and with three children, he accepts a much more remunerative job on commercial television and gradually becomes involved in a life he did not expect.

programme.title: Survivors of the Invisible
programme.desc: One million different species of insects live on Earth. Diving into their world is kind of like adventuring to a faraway and unknown galaxy. With one difference: these living creatures do not live light-years away from us but right under our feet! With unique technologies shots developed by an Austrian entomologist, the film Survivors of the Invisible will make you discover the world of insects as you have never seen it before.

programme.title: Fundamentalism: Is There a Way Back
programme.desc: Is There a Way Back A growing counter-terrorist movement is gaining worldwide momentum.After the attacks in New York, London, Madrid and Bali as well as the assassinations in Toulouse carried out by Mohamed Merah, the world wonders about how these Islamists came to the point they were able to commit such atrocities: to kill in cold blood and be willing to die a Martyr’s death. How and why did these young men become radicals? Is it reversible?In a number of countries, deradicalization programs have sprung up.

programme.title: Boteti: The Returning River
programme.desc: The Returning River For 20 years the Boteti River in northern Botswana lay dry, leaving wildlife dependent on a handful of shrinking rain pools. Then, after decades of drought, heavy rains in the Angolan highlands send water flowing once more. Boteti - The Returning River captures this dramatic rebirth, revealing how animals endured the harsh years and how the river’s return transforms the landscape.

programme.title: Against the Tide
programme.desc: Albert (21) decides to fight cancer on his own terms while striving to help others around the world going through the same traumatic experience.

programme.title: Under the Lights: Pelé - Pele
programme.desc: A biography of the greatest player of all time on the pitch and one of the most iconic legends in sport.

programme.title: Isetenkheb's Egyptian Coffin
programme.desc: Follow from the amazing restoration process of one of the most cherished and mysterious pieces of History: an Egyptian sarcophagus covered with hieroglyphics (painted wood). With exclusive interviews of experts, art curators and restorators, discover everything about the story of the Isetenkheb coffin of Ancient Egypt dated from around 664-500 BC!

programme.title: Travel Thru History - Las Vegas
programme.desc: In this episode we explore Las Vegas’ lesser known past. We visit the National Atomic Testing museum to learn about how the desert outside of Vegas was used for testing America’s secret nuclear weapons. We also visit the Mormon Fort, the first permanent non-native settlement in the area, as well as the Neon Museum.

programme.title: Travel Thru History - Key West
programme.desc: It’s island living in the Keys on this episode of TTH. We learn about the islands treasure hunting history at the Mel Fisher Museum. Then we’ll explore Fort Jefferson, an isolated fort in the Gulf of Mexico that defended the islands. American literature enthusiasts will enjoy a look at Ernest Hemingway’s Key West home, where some of his most famous works were penned.

programme.title: Nature's Force - Episode 7
programme.desc: Weather is universal and it’s also Extra Terrestrial. Learn about space weather and how it can impact us on earth. Supercells are unique storms that scientists have learnt to measure into three types. Under the earth’s crust, nature is extremely energetic, and we see this through the Volcano which acts as our eye into the forces beneath our feet. Learn about the purple buzzing glow called St Elmo’s Fire, how it was named and were to look for it.

programme.title: Nature's Force - Episode 8
programme.desc: The beauty, magic, and the science behind the Auroras at both ends of the earth, show them to be more than just a protective magnetic layer. The technology used to measure Wind Speed is finely calibrated with an interesting formula. The Tides remind us of our connection to the moon and our place in the solar system and are monitored for any significant change can have implications for industry, communities, and our ocean life.

programme.desc: Chennai, formerly known as Madras, can trace its roots back to a tiny fishing village. Bill explores the city’s growth under the British East India Company, with visits to Fort St. George and the Fort Museum. We then travel to the nearby Sao Tome Basilica, the church and burial site of St. Thomas the Apostle. In Pondicherry, French influences can still be felt in the tree-lined streets, colonial mansions and cafés.

programme.title: Journeys in India - Calcutta - City of living history
programme.desc: There is no city in India that is more British than Calcutta. The former capital of British India, Calcutta has gardens, buildings and museums to prove it. Throw away any ideas you have of this giant city and discover the treasures it holds.

programme.title: Journeys in Africa - Kilwa Kisiwani - Swahili King of the Indian Ocean
programme.desc: This ancient ruined city, lost to history, was one of the most powerful in the world during its prime. The architectural sophistication and sheer size will amaze. Then Journeys heads out to the deep ocean for some big game fishing. Will we land the big one or return empty handed?

programme.title: Journeys in Africa - Victoria Falls - The smoke that thunders
programme.desc: One of the 7 Natural Wonders of the World, Victoria Falls is an amazing spectacle that straddles the Zambia/Zimbabwe border. The force of the water is so intense that the water bouncing back creates a rainforest. Remarkably, the wildlife in the area is as abundant as the water going over the falls.

Through the eyes of a cultural academic, a laborer, an architect, an urban planner, and a photographer, the grand evolution of a little fishing village is illustrated and documented to reveal one of the fastest growing megacities in the world.

programme.title: Hidden Traces - 14-18
programme.desc: On the 11th of November, 1918, the First World War drew to an end with a terrible toll… after a conflict unlike anything Humanity had ever seen before. For 4 years and 3 months, soldiers from at least 20 countries were plunged in the hell of trenches… caught under a deluge of bombs.

programme.title: Stolen Treasures - Episode 1
programme.desc: It’s the biggest museum in the world…the museum of artworks stolen over the centuries and never rediscovered. These works haunt the nightmares of their owners, and occupy the days of hundreds of police officers across the world, as well as those of a handful of private agencies; no country or museum of importance can claim to have been spared. According to Interpol, art theft is the fourth largest criminal trade, after the drug trade, the weapons trade and money laundering.

programme.title: The Day When - Hitler Lost the War
programme.desc: Hitler's downfall began before the official end of the war in 1945. Specifically, on June 22, 1941. Hitler launched the largest military offensive in history - against the USSR in Operation Barbarossa.

programme.title: Travel Thru History - Savannah
programme.desc: We visit the old south and enjoy some sweet tea in Savannah. On this episode, we’ll stroll the city’s beautiful squares, as well as visit it’s civil war past at Old Fort Jackson. Then, we head up the stairs of the famous Tybee Island lighthouse and visit the Savannah Railroad museum.

programme.title: Travel Thru History - St. Augustine
programme.desc: There’s a lot to cover in the oldest city in America. Take a sip from the distinctively tasting Fountain of Youth. Then we’ll cross the draw bridge of the undefeated Spanish Fort, the Castillo San Marcos. Then we’ll learn the true history of pirates at the Pirate Museum.

programme.title: Nature's Force - Episode 1
programme.desc: Journey inside Dust Storms to see how they are formed and the hazards and effects they cause. A glimpse into the science of Clouds and how they fit into the weather cycle of the planet. The power of Lightening is more than visual, it is noise, electricity and it even helps plants to grow. Did you know that Rain droplets have different shapes and temperatures, it’s maybe more interesting than you think?

programme.title: Nature's Force - Episode 2
programme.desc: Heatwaves have caused cities to literally meltdown and systems to fail, how are we working with nature’s heat? When two Cyclones collide, we get the Fujiwhara Effect, how is this possible and how does it manifest? Floods occur around the world and the world is learning how to cope, combat and prevent damage and share lessons. How do you classify a Blizzard, and let’s look at some of the worst blizzards that have occurred on earth.

programme.title: Big Coast - Season 12 - Whiskey Cove Chinook
programme.desc: Trolling cut plug herring from home base on Denny Island, BC!

programme.title: Wild Australia with Ray Mears - Episode 4
programme.desc: Ray starts by hitching a lift on a research crane to get a bird’s eye view over the Rainforest; from there, he can see the geographical position responsible for this lush vegetation: mountain range in the west and the sea in the east. He then goes down to the ground, delving into the heart of the jungle, he comes across millennial trees, camouflage spiders and a miniature dinosaur, the Boyd’s Forest Dragon. He pursues his journey by travelling on a zipwire with wildlife expert, Justin McMahon.

programme.title: Journeys in India - Old and New Delhi - A city of contrasts
programme.desc: We explore the capital of India. The bustling metropolis is filled with modern skyscrapers that stand side-by-side with hundreds of ancient monuments, making Delhi a physical dichotomy of yesterday and tomorrow. In the old city, we travel by rickshaw through the narrow streets and discover a world that is quickly disappearing. Then it’s on to the tomb of Humayun, whose architectural design inspired one of the Seven Wonders of the World, the great Taj Mahal.

programme.title: Journeys in India - South India - Land of superlatives
programme.desc: Two of the greatest ancient monuments in the world are in South India—Hampi and Konark. These two wonders of the world were lost to the west, but now are at the top of many bucket lists. Join Bill as he takes the veil off these two incredible achievements of man.

programme.title: Journeys in Africa - Tsavo - Legacy of the Man-Eaters
programme.desc: Featured in films and documentaries, the mane-less lions of Tsavo have a fierce reputation - man-eaters. Journeys embarks on a photo hunt for these legendary beasts of the bush. In the process, we witness the raw power of the ghosts in the dark.

programme.title: Journeys in Africa - Northern Cape - South Africa’s desert
programme.desc: Once a year in good rain years, the deserts of South Africa explode in color. This is the greatest flower bloom in the world. We venture into the desert to experience this first-hand and film the rare animals that call this arid land home.

programme.title: Nomads - Mountain Biking Mexico
programme.desc: Pro mountain bikers take to the rocky mountain terrain of Mexico’s Copper Canyon for the ride of their life.

programme.title: Nomads - Alaska - Big Mountain Heli-Skiing in Haines
programme.desc: X games medalists take to the slopes of Haines, Alaska to experience the ultimate in heli-skiing; a challenge to even the best of the best.

programme.title: Dream Journey - Dream Journey : Mexico, Cancún
programme.desc: Mexico, Cancún February 2017 saw me embark upon a travel expedition through Scotland, Poland, France, Mexico, Belize and, (alas!), back. Not only was it the first time I ventured out to Central America, but also the first time I seriously pushed my bravery boundaries to do a whole lot of things I'd never tried before. I defeated my life-long fear of scubadiving and skydiving, (the Carribbean vistas do help!

programme.title: Of Boats and Men - Episode 1
programme.desc: Travelling by boat bears a priceless sense of Freedom and offers endless new vistas to all passengers. Across waterways around the world Boats are an essential tool of daily life whether they carry goods, serve as utilities or services in remote areas.

programme.title: The Blue Realm - Shark Business
programme.desc: Shark Business unravels some of the mysteries surrounding sharks with controversial behaviorist Dr. Erich Ritter. You'll witness divers testing the limits of shark-human interaction outside of cages with dangerous sharks such as lemon, bull and even great white sharks! Recount the events that led to the attack that almost killed Dr. Ritter. Witness a feeding Frenzy of over 100 reef sharks in the Bahamas, and see a diver literally ride a Great White Shark in Gansbai, South Africa!

programme.title: Blue World - Sand Tiger Sharks + Marine Biology in Turks & Caicos
programme.desc: Jonathan heads down to the shipwrecks of North Carolina (USA) to observe how these wrecks have become home to thousands of animals, including Sand Tiger sharks. But instead of chasing all the fish, the sharks are protecting many of them! Then, Jonathan visits the School for Field Studies in the Turks & Caicos Islands to learn how college students conduct fieldwork in their pursuit of degrees in Marine Studies. He helps tag sharks, study conch and investigate marine protected areas!

programme.title: Blue World - Tonic Immobility in the Bahamas + Diving with Nasa
programme.desc: In a shark-filled adventure, Jonathan travels to the Bahamas to meet Neal Harvey, a world-renown shark handler who will attempt to teach Jonathan how to put Caribbean Reef sharks into a relaxed state known as tonic immobility! Then, Jonathan heads to NASA’s Neutral Buoyancy Lab in Houston, Texas (USA), where astronauts train for space walking underwater, in a giant pool about half the size of a soccer field.

programme.title: Animal Embassy - Morgan the Orce Has a Baby
programme.desc: For over a year, the staff at Loro Parque have been patiently waiting for a huge event to take place. Morgan, the deaf orca is about to give birth to her very first calf. The stakes are high, and the staff are holding their collective breath as the scene is set for the greatest natural phenomenon in the zoo’s history.

programme.title: Animal Embassy - Super Vet to the Rescue
programme.desc: As Loro Parque’s head vet, Jorge never knows from one day to the next what will come through his clinic. From tending to oversexed otters, fine-footed flamingoes or armoured armadillos, a day spent with Jorge, is a day immersed in nature from the four corners of the globe. Ever seen a grown man hug a turtle? For Javier, Loro Parque’s Head of Environmental Affairs, it’s all part of the job!

programme.title: Wild Ones - Venomous
programme.desc: The most venomous snake on land. The deserted heart of the Australian outback, where people seldom venture, is the hot, baked home of the most venomous land snake in the world - the inland taipan, a two meter long snake with enough venom in one bite to kill a quarter of a million mice. Gila Monster - North America’s largest land lizard, venomous and striking, lives in desert regions. Blue-Ringed Octopus - Tiny but deadly, it carries two venoms—one lethal to humans.

programme.title: Wild Ones - Migration
programme.desc: Wildebeest & Zebra - Africa’s iconic drifters. No two zebra have the same stripes, even in vast herds. Olive Ridley Turtles - The world’s most abundant sea turtle, migrating vast distances to nest. Sooty Tern - These seabirds may stay airborne for years before returning to land to breed. Australian Pelicans - Big-billed birds that follow inland waterways in search of fish. Whales & Whale Sharks - Ocean giants that roam the seas, some on epic migrations we barely understand.

programme.title: Race of Life - The Race Underfoot
programme.desc: Insects may be small, but their survival strategies are fierce. They thrive in diverse environments thanks to their exoskeletons, which protect against impact, chemicals, and water. Wings help them escape danger or seek food and mates. Dragonflies hover and dart after prey, monarchs undergo stunning metamorphosis, and praying mantises blend into greenery before striking. Social insects like ants and bees live in colonies.

programme.title: Race of Life - The Race of Life After the Dark
programme.desc: Finally for this series, we are exploring the world of nocturnal animals—creatures adapted to thrive in darkness. Escaping predators, avoiding heat, and sharing resources, they emerge as night falls. Join porcupines, raccoons, mice, cats, foxes, and more on their nightly journey. From raccoons with sensitive touch to mice surviving in teams, each is a master of the night. Across continents, these animals—like the fruit-loving porcupine—showcase fear, excitement, and survival in the shadows.

programme.title: Africa's Deadliest - Episode 2
programme.desc: Killer armies collaborate to take down larger prey. On land, a zebra’s kick can kill, but in the water it’s easy meat for a congregation of crocodiles. Wild dogs may not seem like fearsome predators, but a pack kills fast, brutally and often.

programme.title: Creative Killers - Coliseum
programme.desc: Savuti is big cat country, where only the most resourceful predators thrive. This film follows three characters through winter as small game vanishes and buffalo arrive. The Marsh Pride faces tough terrain and rival lions, while Saba, the matriarch, struggles after a hyena attack. A lone female leopard adapts her hunting strategy to survive in a lion-dominated landscape. Through nighttime hunts and clever use of terrain, these predators battle Savuti’s harsh conditions and each other.

Under every rock, behind every tree, death could be lurking.Africa’s largest cobra is beat to the chase by the Giant bullfrog. Big Brown Bats use sonar to take out Wax moths at high speed. And the world’s 2nd fastest cat leaps 10 feet into the air after its aerial prey.When death comes to the underworld, it takes the express!

You'll travel to the remote Socorro Islands off Mexico's Pacific coast and see breath-taking encounters with enormous manta rays. You're sure to love these majestic giants as you see how they invite human contact, and encourage certain divers to ride them.

Now we follow the aquarium team as they initiate their very own breeding program with the hope of finding many more Nemos to come. Jorge has got a 200-pound problem on his hands. Lin Mao the white tiger has something wrong with his hip and the vets need to make a diagnosis.

programme.desc: Marvel at the site of America’s most famous water dam. We’ll learn about how the Hoover Dam was built, why it’s necessary, and take a behind the scenes look at its inner workings.

programme.title: Nature's Force - Episode 3
programme.desc: A snapshot of Seasons, how they work together and keep the globe in balance. Droughts are explored in terms of how we can predict them, proof our lives from them and collect data because of them. Hurricanes are explained, their power revealed and the measures that are used to help us survive their impact. Thunderstorms have a few stages of development that roll out in a particular order.

programme.title: Nature's Force - Episode 4
programme.desc: How are Rainbows formed and what’s their science? We look at the largest Hail ever recorded and explain why it comes in so many shapes and sizes. Global Warming is a big issue and topic, and we give a nutshell insight to its meaning and impact on many levels. Forecasting is key and crucial to living with nature and its weather, as it involves precision technologies and expertise.

programme.desc: Chasing big Chinook Salmon just outside Rivers Inlet, BC from Duncanby Lodge!

programme.desc: Ray takes the Great Ocean Road along the Antarctic facing coast of Australia - the longest South facing coastline in the world. He starts in Port Philp Bay the entrance to Melbourne Harbour where for the first time he sees a strange marine creature - the weedy sea dragon - a relative of the sea horse. He also swims with a unique species of dolphin - the Burrunan Dolphins.

programme.desc: Sarah travels to one of the top 10 dive destinations in Australia (Julian Rocks, Byron Bay, NSW) to dive with three species of Wobbegong Sharks within the Cape Byron Marine Park. She also conducts a street poll with members of the public to find out what they think about sharks.

programme.title: Journeys in India - Udaipur and Jaipur - India’s natural beauties
programme.desc: Whether you refer to Udaipur as the City of Lakes or the City of Dawn, you are sure to agree that romance and beauty fill the air. While traveling by boat, we visit the many palaces and temples on the shore. We also tour the majestic City Palace and the Garden of the Maids of Honor. In Jaipur, we tour the Pink City, paying close attention to such architectural treasures as the Palace of Winds (Hawa Mahal) and the Amber Fort. We also visit the magnificent collections housed in the City Palace.

programme.title: Journeys in India - Great caves of Ajanta and Ellora
programme.desc: Caves have held a special place in human development. The Hindu, Buddhist and Jain caves in these two UNESCO sites contain some of the most beautiful carvings and paintings found in Asia. This episode explores the history and relationship between these religions.

programme.title: Journeys in Africa - Mombasa - The center of it all
programme.desc: Gold, ivory and slaves drove the economy of the East coast of Africa 500 years ago. Join us as we explore the Portuguese and Arab roles in these horrific trade schemes. We’ll also investigate the pristine waters off the coast of the nearby National Park where our host dons a snorkel mask and comes face-to-face with the creatures of the coral reef.

programme.title: Journeys in Africa - Durban - City of diversity
programme.desc: Few people know that Gandhi got his political activist start in South Africa. This is a city where Asia meets Africa and is one of the most diverse cities in the world. Here Journeys encounters people of European, Far Eastern and Indian descent as well as the local Zulus.

programme.desc: An international team kayaks the classic runs of New Zealand’s south island and in turn they find a new adventure around every bend.

programme.title: Nomads - Snowmobiling the Rocky Mountains
programme.desc: The biggest stars of snowmobile head to the Rocky Mountains for an epic adventure.

programme.title: New Frontier - From There to Here
programme.desc: Series introduction and the study of Earth from orbit. The sky above is littered with stars and countless galaxies. It is where we come from and where we are destined to return. The first phase of this journey is complete, now commences the second, with robotics, advanced technologies and sheer daring we are now going where before we only dreamt.

programme.title: New Frontier - Return to the Moon
programme.desc: The Moon, our closest celestial companion. Our indispensible dance partner through the cosmos. Lighting our night sky and gently tugging at our shores. Few have walked on her surface, though her allure remains strong, once again we are glancing her way with renewed interest and with a view to return very soon.

programme.title: Everyday Elements - Chlorine, Titanium, Gallium, Potassium, Nickel
programme.desc: A series that puts chemistry in our everyday experience by showing the living connection we have with the chemicals and elements that make up our world. The matter that built skies and seas, the atoms that make up you and me, the chemistry around us that forms the things we touch, smell and see. This series shows us what the objects in our universe and in our homes are made from and why the particles around us behave as they do. Everything around us is built from Everyday Elements.

programme.title: Wow, I Never Knew That! - Coca cola, slinky, frisbee
programme.desc: Coca Cola, Slinky, Frisbee Learn how a pharmacist and an accountant created the most famous drink in the world, coca cola! And, learn the “Bear” truth behind how a U.S. president helped create everyone’s favorite stuffed toy, The Teddy Bear! Then, how did a piece of wire accidentally “Slink” its way to become a fantastic fun toy for children? Plus, how a the wiffle ball was invented.

programme.title: Wow, I Never Knew That! - Etch a sketch, bingo, bikini
programme.desc: Coca Cola, Slinky, Frisbee Before computer drawing programs, there was a toy that if you mastered its two circular white knobs you could have a picture perfect sketch. We’ll explain how the etch a sketch drew onto the scene. And what did Neil Armstrong really say when he stepped on the moon, the “aahh” answer will surprise you! Plus, where did the explosive name bikini come from?

programme.title: Water: H2O Stories - The Sorcerer’s Apprentice
programme.desc: H2O Stories - The Sorcerer’s Apprentice Water: H2O Stories is a 3x52 series revisiting the story of water on planet Earth and its disrupted course over time which has led to the 21st century biggest challenge.

programme.title: Inside Outer Space - Milky Way, Enecladus, Saturn, Tides, Eclipse, Looking into the Past
programme.desc: Come with us as we explore and unravel the mysteries of what lies beyond our planet Earth. This is a series packed with space stories and information about our universe covering what we can see, how we can live in space and what science tells us about the past and the future as we journey inside out of space.

programme.title: Nature's Force - Episode 2
programme.desc: Heatwaves have caused cities to literally meltdown and systems to fail, how are we working with nature’s heat? When two Cyclones collide, we get the Fujiwhara Effect, how is this possible and how does it manifest? Floods occur around the world and the world is learning how to cope, combat and prevent damage and share lessons. How do you classify a Blizzard, and let’s look at some of the worst blizzards that have occurred on earth.

programme.title: Everyday Elements - Platinum, Iodine, Aluminum, Iron, Tungsten

programme.title: Quirky Science - Episode 13
programme.desc: Gunpowder, likely discovered by accident, dates back to 300 AD in China. Made from sulfur, charcoal, and saltpeter—found on aged waste—it was hard to produce but vital for rulers. Its explosive power comes from fast-burning gases. Early gunpowder created thick smoke until Nobel invented smokeless ballistite in 1888. The bacteria behind saltpeter’s potency were only understood centuries later. Now, gunpowder may soon be replaced—what’s next?
